correctness.rationale: Determinant of the explicit 4x4 Sylvester matrix gives R=(af+cd)^2+(ae+bd)(bf+ce) over F2. Differentiating in six coordinates yields (eU,eV,eW,bU,bV,bW), with R already in this ideal, and U,W in (b,e), so J=I^2+(b,e)I. Segre minors prime; I^2⊂J⊂I proves radical I; a=1 coordinate change gives local V^2+bUV+cU^2 and ideal (U,V)∩(b,U,V)^2. Globally I/J=(I/I^2)|_T, rank-two conormal of P1xP2 restricted to P1xline, whose splitting has bidegrees (-2,-2),(-2,-1). Independently computed modular resultant and derivatives, full symbolic Groebner basis (7 elements), Hilbert coefficients [1,6,21,50,96,162,251,366] for degrees 0..7 matching given rational series. The geometric interpretation follows from the separately checked Segre normal geometry, not solely from code.

value.rationale: The singular scheme of an elementary universal resultant is not merely its classical Segre rank-drop support: its square-zero conormal embedded component is a genuine scheme-theoretic invariant in small characteristic. The exact sheaf, supporting quadric, and Hilbert series are structurally meaningful tools for studying modular discriminantal geometry, not a cheap Jacobian vanishing check.

final_claim: For two universal binary quadratics over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two, their resultant hypersurface R=V^2+UW in P^5 has Jacobian singular ideal J=I^2+(b,e)I, I=(U,V,W). Reduced support Z=Segre(P^1 x P^2), with a square-zero embedded conormal sheaf supported on T=Segre(P^1 x P^1), equal to O_T(-2,-2) plus O_T(-2,-1). Its Hilbert series is (1-6t^3+6t^4-t^6)/(1-t)^6.
limitations: Only alg-closed characteristic 2; not a claim for positive characteristic different from 2 or characteristic zero.
Hilbert numerator checked symbolically by independent Groebner computation, full Hilbert series follows from its monomial initial ideal, not finite coefficient matching alone.
